batchName: Empire: Tiberius and Caligula (AD 14-41) - Latin words
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What did the soldiers’ nickname Caligula mean?
questions.explanation: As a toddler he wore a miniature uniform with little army boots (caligae).
questions.sourceQuote: the soldiers nicknamed him Caligula, "little boot".

questions.question: What were the aquilae that Germanicus recovered?
options: The eagles, the sacred standards of the legions
questions.explanation: Two of the three eagles lost in the Teutoburg Forest came home.
questions.sourceQuote: recovered two of the three lost eagles (*aquilae*), the sacred standards of the legions.

questions.question: What was a triumphus, like the one Germanicus celebrated in AD 17?
options: A gift of land to soldiers
questions.explanation: Germanicus celebrated his on 26 May AD 17.
questions.sourceQuote: he celebrated a triumph (*triumphus*), a victory parade through Rome.

questions.question: Sejanus was praefectus praetorio. What was that?
questions.explanation: The Guard was the emperor’s bodyguard, and Tiberius moved it into Rome itself.
questions.sourceQuote: Sejanus became praetorian prefect (*praefectus praetorio*) in AD 15

questions.question: What was the corona civica that Tiberius refused?
questions.explanation: He also refused the title Father of the Fatherland.
questions.sourceQuote: the Civic Crown (*corona civica*), an oak-leaf wreath of honour.

questions.question: Caligula reopened old maiestas trials in AD 39. What was the charge?
questions.explanation: He had claimed he had burned Tiberius’s files without reading them.

questions.question: What would damnatio memoriae have done to Caligula?
questions.explanation: His uncle, the new emperor, refused, though many statues were quietly recarved.

questions.question: The new emperor refused to declare Caligula a hostis. What is a hostis?
questions.sourceQuote: refused to declare his nephew a public enemy (*hostis*)
